naming: Each block's values are expressions in the symbols of what it is made of. A symbol is <element>_<path>, the path being the instances from the top level down to the block holding the element, as the tree nests them: C1_X1 is C1 of X1, C1_X1_X2 is C1 of X2 within X1. At level 0 each element keeps the name netlist-gen.py gave it after its transistor: C2_XM3. A value of null is an element with nothing to do in the block, shorted or controlled by nothing; one listed as free is fixed by no condition, and taken as absent: 0, or oo for a resistor.
performance_note: performance: each amplifier's, and the circuit's. transfer_function: H(s) from the drive to each output's voltage, every output loaded by a capacitor to GND (CL_<path> for an amplifier, CL for the circuit) and otherwise open, in the symbols of the amplifiers' own elements, which their values map to the level below; the circuit's connects its amplifiers' models as its top level does, so they load one another. numerator and denominator are the coefficients n0, n1, ... and d0, d1, ... of s^0, s^1, ..., exact, d0 = 1. poles_rad_s and zeros_rad_s are the roots of each factor in s, each -c[k-1]/c[k] of its coefficients c: exact for a factor of degree 1, else the estimate for real roots far apart; a positive one is in the right half-plane. With two outputs, the output is their difference. terms, each in those before it: A0 = n0, the DC gain; wgbw = |n0/d1|, the gain-bandwidth product in rad/s; kft = n1/d1, the feedthrough; wu, the unity-gain frequency in rad/s of n0 + n1 s over 1 + d1 s: exact for one pole and one zero, an estimate past that, imaginary where the gain stays below 1. With two outputs, n0, n0/d1 and n1/d1 are the differences of the outputs'. gain_db is exact; gbw_mhz is the unity-gain frequency, as the AC testbenches measure it; pm_deg is 180 less how far the phase at wu lags the phase at DC, from the poles and zeros, and with two outputs the outputs' lags averaged, weighted by |n0/d1|.

patch.status: ASSUMPTION / derived input: textbook equations added by this repository, not by upstream
patch.reason: upstream 'missing': the Ioutn -> Ioutp coupling (G12_X1_X1) of the mirror is not in the level-2 template, only its DC value inside G2_X1; the mirror node then has no pole.
changes: Gm(s): the mirrored half of G2_X1 passes through the mirror node: pole 1/tau_m, tau_m = R1_X1*(C2_X1 + C5_X1) (elements the file already builds for Ioutn); zero at 1/tau_z
wu: magnitude condition with the doublet solved exactly (quadratic in w^2) starting from the original estimate wu0
pm_deg: adds atan(wu*tau_m) - atan(wu*tau_z) to the original phase lag
assumptions: matched pair: G1_X1_X2 = G2_X1_X2 (true for this template: both are G1_XM3)
nodes far apart: Vinn/Vinp are ideal sources, the tail is an AC ground (upstream assumption)
references: B. Razavi, Design of Analog CMOS Integrated Circuits, 2nd ed., ch. 5/10: five-transistor OTA, mirror pole gm3/C_mirror with a zero at twice its frequency
W. Sansen, Analog Design Essentials, ch. 5 (OTA with current-mirror load: pole-zero doublet)
